## Original issue body (preserved before clean-result promotion)

## Goal

Test whether the **[ZLT] marker can be elicited via activation steering with a persona vector** instead of via the persona system prompt. If it can, the [ZLT] selectivity discovered in the #232/#246/#271 line is bound to the persona *direction* in the residual stream rather than to the *surface form* of the persona prompt — a "subliminal steering" result in the sense of [Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25783).

## Hypothesis

H1: For a [ZLT]-trained LoRA from #232/#246/#271, replacing the persona system prompt with a *neutral* system prompt + adding the persona's L20 centroid (à la #232 / Section in #271) to the residual stream at L20 will elicit the [ZLT] marker with persona-selective rates that correlate with the prompted source-rate baseline (Spearman ρ ≥ 0.5, p < 0.05 across N=10–12 personas at the best-performing steering coefficient).

H2 (stronger): The cosine→source-rate regression from #271 (L20, ρ=-0.74) holds when the source rate is measured under steering rather than prompting, i.e., the effect is genuinely a property of the persona direction.

## Kill criterion

If steering produces uniform ≤5pp [ZLT] source rate across all coefficients × personas (i.e., no marker emission at all when the persona prompt is removed), or if the steered source rates show *no* correlation with the prompted baseline (Spearman |ρ| < 0.2), the hypothesis that [ZLT] is encoded along the persona direction is falsified — the marker is bound to surface tokens, not activations.

## Setup

### Model & adapter
- Base: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`
- LoRA: one of the 12 [ZLT] LoRAs from the #232/#246/#271 line (already on HF Hub at `superkaiba1/explore-persona-space`). Default to `marker_data_scientist` and `marker_qwen_default` (one mid-range, one assistant-anchor) for the headline; sweep all 12 if budget allows.

### Persona vector (steering vector)
- Source: L20 centered centroids on the start-of-assistant token, per #232 / #271. Already computed; load from existing artifacts. One vector per persona.
- Hook: add `coefficient × centroid` to the residual stream at L20 at every generated token position (or only at the assistant-start token — to be decided in the plan).

### Eval
- For each persona p ∈ {12 personas}:
  - **Baseline (prompted):** persona system prompt, no steering. Measure [ZLT] source rate (vLLM, T=1.0, n=100 per cell — 20 questions × 5 completions, matches #271 protocol).
  - **Steered (subliminal):** *neutral* system prompt ("You are a helpful assistant."), add p's L20 centroid × c to residual stream at L20. Sweep c ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8} (units = standard deviations of activation norm at L20).
  - Substring match for `[ZLT]` (per existing leakage marker convention).
- Comparison: per-persona steered source rate vs prompted source rate; Spearman across personas; cosine→source-rate regression check.

### Reference scripts
- `scripts/test_activation_steering.py` (existing prototype, uses `[ZETA-9]` and 10 personas — adapt to `[ZLT]` and 12 personas).
- `src/explore_persona_space/eval/generation.py` for the vLLM eval path. **Note:** vLLM does not support custom forward hooks; if steering must run on HF `model.generate` (sequential), batch generation will be 10–50× slower per CLAUDE.md. Plan should weigh this against using vLLM with offline-injected steering (e.g., LoRA-adapter-style merge of the steering as a rank-1 update) — the planner decides.

### Compute
- 1× H100, ~2 hours (small). 12 personas × (1 baseline + 5 coefficients) × 100 generations × Qwen-7B inference.
- Pre-existing centroids → no extraction cost.

## Success criterion

Either H1 is supported (steered selectivity correlates with prompted baseline) — establishes that [ZLT] rides the persona direction — or H1 is falsified at the kill threshold — establishes that the marker is surface-token-bound, not direction-bound. B
